issues.details: Rubric only accepts “fiber or dietary fiber” while the prompt asks for a carbohydrate; calibration items typically allow common equivalents (e.g., cellulose, insoluble fiber). Rubric should be broadened or prompt narrowed to match expected answers.
Item is extremely basic definitional recall; still within range but on the easier side compared with many source FRQs that often require a bit more application or specificity.

Omega-number conversion is acceptable given calibration (e.g., omega-3/omega-6 numeric items), but the stem is more tutorial than needed for this level; could be shortened to match the concise style of the alpha-linolenic/DHA examples.

Two-point FRQ with two conceptual elements is acceptable, but the scenario is somewhat verbose relative to calibration short-answer items and edges toward explanation rather than concise identification. Could be tightened while preserving the two requested facts.

Three-point explanatory FRQ with multi-sentence mechanistic explanation is more elaborate than typical Division B 2022 calibration FRQs, which are usually single fact/number or very short conceptual descriptions. This reads more like an extended free-response than the short-answer style shown in the corpus.

Rubric breaks explanation into three subpoints for a single short-answer prompt; calibration rubrics for similar items (e.g., Biuret description) are simpler and less segmented. This level of granularity is not strictly source-faithful.

Four-point naming FRQ is heavier-weight than typical Division B 2022 short-answer items, which are usually 1–3 points and often numeric or single-concept. The multi-mark structure for simple recall is not well supported by calibration examples.
Assigning 4 points to straightforward vitamin-letter recall inflates its weight relative to its conceptual difficulty and compared with source FRQs of similar content.

Concept and format are reasonable, but the explanatory style (label interpretation with narrative context) is slightly more wordy than most calibration numeric/short-answer label questions, which tend to be more direct. Still acceptable but could be more concise.

Very close in content and phrasing to calibration item uchicago-test-22 (Biuret reaction description). While not verbatim, it targets essentially the same explanation at similar difficulty, reducing novelty of the bank.

Two-point mechanistic explanation is acceptable, but the rubric’s emphasis on detailed coordination-complex language is more advanced/chemistry-heavy than typical Division B expectations, edging toward Division C depth.

Density = mass/volume calculation with no food-specific twist is functionally identical to generic physics/chemistry practice and less contextual than the Troy calibration items, which use more realistic industrial volumes and unit conversions. This violates the instruction to avoid needless or purely decorative calculation.
While density calculations appear in calibration, they are more involved (unit conversions, non-trivial context). This item is too trivial and decontextualized for the event’s style.

Several FRQs (e.g., curated-frq-001, -002, -004) adopt extended, multi-mark explanatory rubrics more reminiscent of long-form free-response than the concise, single-fact or short numeric answers seen in the 2022 Division B calibration set. Overall FRQ bank is not fully source-faithful in response length and rubric style.
